judged_text: zoho-bigin passes the credential row ID (credentialId) to refreshOAuthTokens where a user ID is required — the third parameter is documented and used as calcomUserId, and every other app passes credential.userId — so the parent application will look up the wrong user (or none), returning another user's tokens that get persisted onto the wrong Cal.com user's credential (cross-user credential contamination) or simply breaking the sync feature for this app.

record.issue_text: zoho-bigin passes the credential row ID (credentialId) to refreshOAuthTokens where a user ID is required — the third parameter is documented and used as calcomUserId, and every other app passes credential.userId — so the parent application will look up the wrong user (or none), returning another user's tokens that get persisted onto the wrong Cal.com user's credential (cross-user credential contamination) or simply breaking the sync feature for this app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the third argument (`userId`) is used as `calcomUserId` in the POST body (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call passes `credentialId` as that third parameter (`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`), whereas other integrations consistently pass `credential.userId`. If `credentialId` is the credential row ID (as its name implies), the sync endpoint will receive the wrong Cal.com user identifier, causing sync to fail or associate refreshed tokens with the wrong user in the parent app.
